subject: maths
source: NCERT Ganita Prakash | Grade 6, Chapter 4 + BHPS midterm model paper (2026-27)

topics.name: Drawing bar graphs and choosing a scale

questions.q: Facts, numbers, measures and observations that give information are called…
questions.e: Data can be organised in tables using tally marks.

questions.q: Frequency means…
questions.a: the number of times a value occurs
questions.e: Frequency = count of occurrences.

questions.q: How is the number 5 shown with tally marks?
questions.a: Four lines with a fifth line across them
questions.e: Bundling in fives makes counting quick.

questions.q: Why do we organise raw data in a frequency table?
questions.a: So it is easy to read, compare and interpret
questions.e: A tally/frequency table summarises the data at a glance. (Model paper Q34.)

questions.q: In a pictograph, the key (scale) tells us…
questions.a: how many items each picture stands for
questions.e: Always read the key before counting.

questions.q: Key: one symbol = 5 students. How many students do 5 symbols show?
questions.e: 5 × 5 = 25. (Model paper Q30a.)

questions.q: Key: one symbol = 4 books. How is 10 books shown?
questions.a: 2 full symbols and half a symbol
questions.e: 10 ÷ 4 = 2½ symbols.

questions.q: Key: one symbol = 2 books. Anu read 16 books. How many symbols should be drawn for Anu?
questions.e: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 symbols. (Model paper Q32.)

questions.q: A graph that uses bars of equal width to show data is a…
questions.e: (Model paper Q4.)

questions.q: Bars in a bar graph can be drawn vertically or…
questions.e: (Model paper Q6.)

questions.q: In a bar graph, the length (or height) of a bar shows the…
questions.e: Longer bar → larger value.

questions.q: In a bar graph, all bars should have…
questions.a: the same width and equal gaps between them
questions.e: Only the length should change, so the comparison is fair.

questions.q: The first step when drawing a bar graph is to…
questions.a: choose a scale and draw and label the axes
questions.e: Axes, labels and scale come first.

questions.q: Values 12, 16, 20, 24 and 20 are to be drawn as bars. Which scale is best?
questions.e: All values are multiples of 4, and the bars stay a sensible length. (Model paper Q28.)

questions.q: For very large numbers (like thousands of people), which is usually better?
questions.a: A bar graph with a suitable scale
questions.e: Drawing thousands of symbols is impractical; a bar graph with a scale works well.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The scale must be written on every bar graph.
Reason (R): Without the scale, a reader cannot convert bar lengths into values.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
w: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.e: Both true; R explains why the scale is necessary.

questions.q: Pictograph key: one symbol = {k} children. The ‘Art Club’ row has {s} full symbols and one half symbol. How many children?
questions.e: {s} × {k} + half of {k} = {ans}.

questions.q: In a pictograph one symbol stands for {k} books. How many symbols are needed to show {v} books?
questions.e: {v} ÷ {k} = {ans} symbols – draw {m} full symbols and a half.

questions.q: Why is ‘1 symbol = 3 fish’ a poor key when the data are 10, 20 and 25?
questions.a: None of the values divides exactly by 3, so you need awkward part-symbols
questions.e: Choose a key that divides the data neatly – here 5 works.

questions.q: The largest value in your data is {v}. The graph paper has 10 squares. Which is the smallest sensible scale from 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100?
questions.e: The top of the axis (10 × scale) must reach {v}: 1 square = {ans}.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT needed when drawing a bar graph?
questions.a: A different colour for every bar
w: Bars of equal width with equal gaps
questions.e: Colours are optional; title, scale and equal widths are essential.

questions.q: A bar graph’s vertical axis starts at 50 instead of 0. Why can this mislead?
questions.a: Small differences look much bigger than they are
questions.e: Always check where the scale starts before comparing bar heights.

questions.q: A tally shows {b} bundles of five and {r} single marks. What number does it show?
{t} students chose one fruit each: {a} chose mango and {c} chose banana; the rest chose apple. How many chose apple?
A bar graph uses 1 square = {s}. The bar for Monday is {m} squares tall and Tuesday is {u} squares. How many more on Monday?
questions.e: ({m} − {u}) squares × {s} = {ans}.
